subtitle: Mira and Pip's illustrated Nothing Hunt

2.alt: An open illustrated book sits beside a round stamp reading Review 1.3.0 and a small magnifying glass.

3.text:
A parcel arrived at Mira's Clue Workshop.
Inside were a map and a note:

FIND NOTHING TO OPEN THE STAR DOOR.
3.alt: Mira and Pip stand beside an open parcel. A recognisable map shows five empty star spaces leading to two closed mystery doors.

4.text:
The map had five empty star spaces.
Each checked clue would light one star.
Five stars would open the mystery doors.
4.subtext: A clue is something you notice that helps you look again. First look, then say, then turn to check.
4.alt: The map is shown clearly with five empty star spaces followed by two closed doors. Four smaller symbols show LOOK, SAY, TURN and CHECK in that order.

5.text:
Mira is in her room.

Can you spot five things?
5.subtext: Look carefully. The next page will name the objects.
5.alt: A recognisable bedroom shows Mira and Pip with a bed and pillow, four-pane window, bookshelf with coloured books, standing lamp, striped rug, box and yellow bell. No object names are shown yet.

6.text:
Mira checked the room with Pip.
Each label named one thing they could see.

The map was ready for Clue One.
6.subtext: This was their practice search. No star had lit yet. A tiny code is hidden on this page.
6.alt: The same bedroom returns with clear labels above MIRA, PIP, BED, WINDOW, BOOKS, LAMP, BOX and BELL. A small gold star sticker hidden near the objects reads ROOMSTAR.

8.text:
The toy was outside the box.
The box was still there.
Mira looked inside.
8.subtext: The box was empty, but Mira could still see it.
8.alt: The toy-box reveal places written labels above MIRA LOOKED, BOX, PIP WATCHED, TOY OUTSIDE and EMPTY INSIDE.

9.text:
A container holds things.
This box is a container.
Empty means the toy is not inside.

Clue One checked: the first star lit.
9.subtext: The empty box is still here. Can you find the tiny hidden code?
9.alt: Pip stands beside a gold clue star and a recognisable box. Their labels are above the pictures. A tiny code hidden on the star reads BOXCLUE.

10.text:
The bell did not ring.

What did Mira and Pip do while they waited?
10.subtext: Cup your hand by your ear and listen with Mira.

11.text:
Mira listened.
Pip waited.
The bell stayed still and quiet.

Clue Two checked: the second star lit.
11.subtext: The bell did not ring, but Mira and Pip were still there. Can you find the tiny hidden code?
11.alt: Labels above the recognisable pictures read MIRA LISTENED, LISTENING, BELL STAYED STILL and PIP WAITED. The tiny code QUIETWINGS is printed on the bell.

12.text:
Pip found a card with no drawing on it.

'Nothing!' he chirped.

What can you spot?
12.subtext: There are four clues before you turn the page.
12.alt: A familiar blank-paper emoji, purple feather, magnifying glass and pencil are shown without names for the child to spot.

13.text:
Mira could see the card, the pencil, Pip's feather and her magnifying glass.

Clue Three checked: the third star lit.
13.subtext: Blank means there is no mark on the card. Can you find the tiny hidden code?
13.alt: Labels above the recognisable pictures read CARD, PENCIL, PIP'S FEATHER and MAGNIFYING GLASS. A tiny code hidden along the card edge reads BLANKEDGE.

14.text:
Pip arranged seven letter blocks.

Can you find the word NOTHING?
14.subtext: Look across the blocks from left to right.

15.text:
The letters spell NOTHING.
We can see and read the word.

Clue Four checked: the fourth star lit.
15.subtext: The word is here, even though it names nothing.

16.text:
Mira put the toys behind a curtain.
Part of each toy was hidden.

Did the room become nothing?
16.subtext: Spot what stayed in the picture.

17.text:
The curtain hid part of each toy.
Mira could still see the curtain, part of the toys and Pip.

Clue Five checked: the fifth star lit.
17.subtext: A view is what we can see from one place. The map was complete. Can you find the tiny hidden code?
17.alt: Labels above the recognisable pictures name MIRA, PIP, CURTAIN and TOYS PARTLY HIDDEN. A tiny code woven into the purple curtain reads CURTAINMAP.

18.text:
All five stars shone on the map.
The star door unlocked.

Behind it stood two mystery doors.
18.subtext: 'Now we can test the note,' said Mira.
18.alt: Mira and Pip hold the completed map with five bright stars. An open star-marked doorway reveals two closed mystery doors beyond it.

19.text:
Door A holds out a card.
Door B does not.

Which door gives Mira something to look at?
19.subtext: Something shown for us to look at is called an example.
19.alt: Labels above the two recognisable doors read DOOR A and DOOR B. Door A has a card beneath it; Door B has an empty dashed frame. The answer labels have not appeared yet.

20.text:
Door A shows Mira the card.
Mira can look at it and point to it.

This card is an example.
20.subtext: An example is something shown for us to look at or check.
20.alt: Door A is shown beside a card and Mira. Labels above the pictures read DOOR A, CARD SHOWN and MIRA LOOKED.

21.text:
Door B did not show Mira a card.
There was no new object from Door B for Mira to look at.
21.subtext: This is what 'no example was given' means. We do not make up a hidden one.
21.alt: Door B is shown beside an empty dashed frame and Mira. Labels above the pictures read DOOR B, NO CARD SHOWN YET and MIRA LOOKED; no secret object appears.

22.text:
Can you draw nothing on this card?

You may make a mark or leave the card blank.
22.subtext: Choose first. Then turn the page to check both choices.

23.text:
If you drew a mark, the mark is here.
If you left it blank, the card is here.

Neither choice made nothing appear.
23.subtext: Mira can still point to the mark or the card.
23.alt: Written labels above the two large pictures read MARK HERE and BLANK CARD HERE.

24.text:
When someone shows us an object, we have something to look at.
When no object is shown, we cannot point to an object from that door.
24.subtext: That is what 'no example was given' means.
24.alt: Mira's detective board places labels above a shown card, something to look at, an empty dashed frame marked NO OBJECT SHOWN YET and Mira keeping both paths.

25.subtext: The parcel's note had led them through every check. Mira and Pip had found the starting clue of Smithian Fold Theory. Can you find the final tiny hidden code?
25.alt: Labels sit above Mira, an open treasure gift, five clue stars and Pip. The tiny code TWODOORS is printed on the gift ribbon.

26.text:
In this game, Mira checks what people show, say, draw or save in a note.

She does not guess about things no one has shown.
26.subtext: A careful detective says what the game can check and where the check stops.
26.alt: A green game mat contains four recognisable symbols with labels above them: SHOW, SAY, DRAW and SAVE IN A NOTE. A stop symbol labelled DO NOT GUESS marks the edge of the game.

27.text:
Find four clues:
an empty box, a still bell, a blank card and a partly hidden toy.
27.subtext: Name each object first. Then say what is empty, still, blank or hidden.

28.text:
Box here - no toy inside.
Bell here - no ring.
Card here - no mark.
Curtain here - toy partly hidden.
28.subtext: Mira named what she could see and what was missing.
28.alt: The final search scene returns with labels above EMPTY BOX, STILL BELL, BLANK CARD, CURTAIN and TOY PARTLY HIDDEN. The teddy remains partly visible below the curtain.

29.text:
Which pictures show an object you can look at?
Which empty frame means no object was shown yet?
29.subtext: Move your finger from each picture or frame to a basket.
29.alt: Three recognisable pictures show a box, bell and blank card. A fourth position is an empty dashed frame. Category labels appear above the two groups: OBJECTS TO LOOK AT and NO OBJECT SHOWN YET.

30.text:
Box, bell and card: objects to look at.
Empty frame: no object was shown yet.
30.subtext: That is what NO EXAMPLE GIVEN means.
30.alt: Labels above the recognisable box, bell and card connect them to OBJECTS TO LOOK AT. A label above the empty dashed frame connects it to NO OBJECT SHOWN YET.

32.text:
Mira closed the first case and placed the completed map in the workshop library.

A new parcel waited: how can ONE whole have many parts?
32.subtext: Next: One Whole, Many Parts - Book E02 and the next game level
